# Morning memo — 2026-08-05

**Source failures (if any):** none reported for this claim batch.

## Worth attention

- **Launch HN: Hoplite (YC S26) – Effortlessly deploy cloud coding agents** — https://hoplite.sh
  YC S26 startup launches a service to deploy coding agents to the cloud, porting over local setup — sessions, memories, MCP servers. Directly adjacent to your own multi-agent setup (Claude Desktop, Codex, Plan Tracker all spawning second-brain children). Worth a look as either a tool or a competitive reference point for cloud-hosted agent fanout.

- **Show HN: Run an 80B Qwen in 4.3 GB of RAM on a Mac, and a 35B on an iPhone** — https://github.com/leonickson1/Swiftlet
  A new quantization/compression approach claims to run an 80B-parameter Qwen model in 4.3GB RAM on Mac hardware, with a 35B variant on iPhone. If the claims hold up this changes the calculus for local inference and could sit alongside your existing Ollama BGE-M3 setup. Unverified claim (Show HN, no independent benchmark yet) — worth testing locally before relying on it.

- **Quoting David Crawshaw's prompt** — https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/3/david-crawshaw/#atom-everything
  A one-line reusable prompt pattern: a nightly cron job that tells a coding agent to fetch upstream changes, rebase local modifications, verify things still work, and replace the current version. This is structurally the same shape as your nightly-librarian pipeline — worth stealing for other repos you maintain forks or vendored copies of.
